summary: Anthropic launched Claude Science, a beta AI workbench that lets researchers run multi-agent scientific workflows across genomics, proteomics and other domains, scaling compute on demand via HPC clusters or Modal.

mechanisms.reason: The product is built around a coordinating agent that spins up specialist sub-agents to perform multi-step research tasks previously done manually with separate tools.
mechanisms.quote: Users interact with a generalist coordinating agent with access to over 60 curated skills and connectors pre-configured for genomics, single-cell, proteomics, structural biology, cheminformatics, and more.

mechanisms.reason: Multi-agent pipelines that spawn sub-agents and run large analyses imply more aggregate compute calls per research task.
mechanisms.quote: scaling the analysis from a single GPU to hundreds as needed.

mechanisms.reason: Sessions hold large datasets and context in memory across multi-step agent workflows, increasing per-session memory footprint.
mechanisms.quote: Because its agents work inside a running session that holds context in memory, even massive datasets only need to be loaded once.

categories.reason: The workbench routes large compute jobs to on-demand GPU hosting via Modal or existing HPC clusters, implying incremental demand for hosted AI compute.
categories.quote: submitting the job to the computing resources your lab already uses (your own HPC cluster over SSH, or your Modal account for compute on demand)
